newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European bourses mixed, markets await Fed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European bourses mixed, markets await Fed.

text.p: German and French stocks recovered their composure on Tuesday after a sharp overnight rebound on Wall Street but London slumped after a bullish start on interest rate concerns.

All share and currency markets were to some degree holding their breath ahead of a decision from a key U.S. monetary policy-making meeting and bourse sentiment was not helped by another weak start by New York stocks.

Dealers and analysts were deeply divided over whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) committee would sanction a credit tightening after the meeting which began at 1300 GMT. Its outcome was not likely to be known until after European markets closed.
If the Fed decided to increase interest rates, it would be the first rise for 1-1/2 years.

British stocks reversed their opening gains with shares in banks, a driving force behind London's recent rally, leading the FTSE index lower. HSBC, Barclays and NatWest led the retreat as fears of a U.S. rate hike prompted profit-taking.

A signal from the Bank of England that it had, as expected, left interest rates unchanged after the government's monthly monetary meeting made little impact on shares. Nor did reports showing a stronger-than-expected 2.2 percent British GDP growth in the second quarter.
"The market felt pretty good this morning but right now it feels horrible," said the head of equity trading at one top brokerage as the FTSE 100 plumbed the day's depths.
Another trader said: "I would think the market would take a quarter-point hike in its stride but at the moment we just don't want to do anything."
In Frankfurt, German shares ended bourse trade higher, although volumes remained generally limited. Dealers said range trade was expected to continue in post-bourse electronic trading.
The DAX index of blue chip shares ended 11.41 points higher at 2,638.45.
On the Paris bourse stocks held their early gains in quiet trading ahead of the Fed decision. Brokers said a quarter-point rise in U.S. interest rates was already priced into the market.

One Paris disappointment was Europe's largest steelmaker Usinor Sacilor, privatised last July. Its shares dropped after it announced first-half profits plunged by 65 percent and warned that its second half earnings would be even weaker. On the currency front, too, the mood was one of wait and see. The dollar was stuck in a tiny range by midday in Europe and dealers said all eyes were on the Fed amid confusion over what impact its decision would have on the market.
A quarter-point rise in the federal funds target rate was largely discounted, but analysts were deeply divided over whether the FOMC would sanction a change in U.S. monetary policy at all.
CURRENCIES AT 1345 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5142 marks and 109.73 yen compared with 1.5120 marks and 109.88 yen in Europe late on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1345 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 9.3 points down at 3,910.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 14.34 points up at 2,081.43.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 11.41 at 2,638.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was higher at $382.55 compared with Monday's London close of $381.25. Silver also fixed firmer at 491.00 cents.
